data.gender_notes: Drishti is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Drishti refers to the ability to see or perceive. It is derived from the Sanskrit word ‘drsh’, which means ‘to see’. In Hindu mythology, Drishti is associated with the goddess Saraswati, the deity of knowledge and wisdom. The name Drishti carries the meaning “Sight, Vision” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Drishti usually hope their child will grow to embody sight, vision and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: The divine power of insight and understanding.
data.etymology: Drishti belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Sight, Vision.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Drishti total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: The term Drishti holds immense cultural significance in the Indian subcontinent, particularly in Hinduism. It is considered an essential aspect of human personality in Indian psychology. In the Indian classical arts such as dance, Drishti refers to the concentrated gaze of the performer towards an audience member, which can lead to a profound connection between the performer and the spectator. This concept highlights the importance of the role of the observer and the interplay between seeing and being seen.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, Drishti symbolizes the inner vision or the capacity to perceive the inner reality beyond the physical world. It reflects the idea that spiritual growth and development require the ability to see beyond the material world and understand the deeper truths of existence. Drishti is also considered a metaphor for concentrate consciousness or focus on the divine. Therefore, in religious and philosophical contexts, Drishti can be seen as a potential gateway to spiritual and self-realization. The goddess Saraswati, who is associated with Drishti, represents the power of knowledge and wisdom that enables one to gain true insight and understanding.
